question: Why do next-token Transformers learn features that are not needed for the immediate prediction, and can their emergence be attributed to direct loss, future-position pre-caching, or parameter sharing across token positions?

key_findings.claim: Author theorem: for a chosen layer and position, the training gradient can be exhaustively partitioned into direct, pre-cached, and circuit-sharing computational paths.
key_findings.evidence: The direct term contains immediate-next-token loss paths through the selected residual stream; the pre-cached term contains later-position losses whose paths traverse it through attention; the shared term contains all remaining paths that affect the same position-shared parameters without traversing that local residual. Proposition 3.1 proves the algebraic sum equals the total gradient for that chosen cut. Exhaustiveness follows from the stop-gradient partition, while the semantic labels remain an interpretive choice tied to that cut.

key_findings.claim: Author method: myopic training ablates pre-caching, m-untied training ablates cross-position circuit sharing, and exact-trajectory replay attributes feature emergence to the three gradient components.
key_findings.evidence: Myopic training stops gradients between a loss position and K/V activations at other positions. m-untied training uses separate parameter sets before and after a split while the latter can still attend to the former cache. For attribution, a final linear-probe direction defines feature mismatch; the model is retrained from identical initialization and data order, and component influences are integrated at every step. Adam uses separate first moments per component but one shared second-moment learning rate so the adjusted components sum to the actual update.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported toy-task result: features that are locally NTP-useless are weakened when both non-direct gradient routes are removed, and a two-layer Conditioned Majority circuit cannot be learned myopically.
key_findings.evidence: Across ten seeds, probe correlations for majority-so-far and previous-token features are lowest in myopic untied models during the random input phase. All non-myopic Conditioned Majority variants score 0.99-1.00, whereas tied and untied myopic models both score about 0.76; Majority remains solvable, though the myopic untied variant falls to 0.96 plus or minus 0.05. The appendix suggests the tied Conditioned Majority model may itself use a less robust shared-gradient shortcut rather than the expected circuit.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported Othello result: board cells that affect legal next moves receive direct training influence and are more linearly recoverable, while other occupied cells still receive pre-cached and shared influence.
key_findings.evidence: In a six-layer OthelloGPT, the probe gap between NTP-useful and NTP-useless squares is positive and grows with depth. The 95% intervals show positive direct influence only for useful squares, while shared influence is positive for both and pre-cached influence is positive for useless squares. This refines, but does not overturn, prior evidence that legal-move-equivalent boards have fragile internal state: the experiment uses one training seed and reports noisy, nonstationary position effects.

anchors.section: Probe methodology and noisy position effects

key_findings.claim: Author-reported TinyStories result: blocking pre-caching raises language-model loss but barely changes simple syntax probes, while an original-story-position feature receives pre-cached influence in middle layers.
key_findings.evidence: Four-layer, 128-dimensional models trained for 1,000 steps over 256,000 TinyStories samples yield loss 3.29 plus or minus 0.02 with myopic training versus 2.53 plus or minus 0.10 normally across ten seeds. POS and dependency probes are similar and direct influence dominates at every layer; pre-cached influence dominates the positional feature in middle layers. The title-level claim that pre-caching is required for coherent text is inferred from loss and samples from tiny models, not a human coherence evaluation.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported large-model result: a local intervention proxy identifies Gemma-2 SAE features whose delayed-to-immediate effect ratio has heavy tails enriched for formal structure.
key_findings.evidence: For 14,565 retained features from the Gemma Scope layer-15 16k SAE, Q(w) is the sum of future-position KL changes divided by immediate-position KL after feature ablation. Features classified as code/math/syntax have fitted log-normal scale 1.63 plus or minus 0.03 versus 1.23 plus or minus 0.02 for other features; steering high-Q features produces more code-like and punctuation-heavy samples. Labels originate from GPT-4o-mini descriptions classified by GPT-4.1-nano. Q(w) is a well-defined intervention statistic, but the separate Proposition 5.1 claim that it approximates a gradient-influence ratio is not established by the appendix proof.

anchors.section: D.4-D.5 SAE filtering and automated labels

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: Proposition 5.1's proof does not establish that the delayed-to-immediate KL ratio Q(w) approximates the corresponding parameter-gradient influence ratio.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 10 correctly introduces a Jacobian Gram metric between the feature direction and each loss gradient, but then treats that matrix as though it were a common scalar multiplying the activation-space inner product used in Equation 11. A general Jacobian Gram matrix cannot be factored out of an inner product or cancelled between direct and pre-cached directions without an additional isotropy, eigenvector, or proportionality assumption. First-order expansion and perfect model fit convert activation-space loss changes to KL divergences but do not remove this metric mismatch. Q(w) therefore remains an empirical local delayed/immediate effect ratio, not a proved estimator of historical gradient influence.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the paper's linear look-ahead experiment does not show a robust uniformly negative relationship between Q(w) and future-token information.
key_findings.evidence: The authors train linear maps from Gemma residuals to tokens up to five positions ahead and correlate each map's leading right-singular subspace alignment with SAE directions' Q(w). The Spearman curves in Figure 7 and Pearson curves in Figure 20 are rank-dependent, small over much of the range, and cross or approach zero for some ranks; no uncertainty intervals or significance tests are given. The result argues against a strong positive association in this particular linear/SAE test, but it is weaker than the prose's 'strong evidence' for a general breadcrumb account.

anchors.section: 5.2 Pre-caching and look-ahead are separate phenomena / Figure 7

key_findings.claim: Negative result: steering validates the formal-structure association only for high Q(w), not symmetrically for the low-Q tail that also drives the fitted heavy-tail result.
key_findings.evidence: The distribution analysis groups both extreme tails as formal-feature enriched, and Table 7 includes several code-related descriptions among the ten lowest-Q features. Yet the authors explicitly report that low-Q steering does not produce the same code or punctuation effect as high-Q steering; Figure 19 shows the clear increase only in the greater-than-10 bin. Thus steering is a one-sided validation of high delayed influence, not causal confirmation of the full two-tail semantic association.

key_findings.claim: Negative result: the myopic Othello intervention is also an optimization failure, so its lower board-state decodability is not a selective test of pre-caching alone.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix Figure 9 states that the myopic OthelloGPT run is much less stable and does not converge to the non-myopic model's loss or accuracy; Figure 10 then shows its weaker board probes. Because the experiment uses one model seed and changes the learnable multi-layer circuit class, the probe gap can reflect broad undertraining or optimization instability in addition to removal of pre-cached gradients.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: the framework usefully separates a feature's final causal role from the gradient routes that created it, but its large-model proxy cannot recover training provenance and its feature ontology is task- and probe-dependent.
key_findings.evidence: Exact influence attribution requires a second identical training trajectory and final linear probes, making it practical only for small models. For Gemma, Q(w) measures local output sensitivity after an SAE intervention, not integrated historical gradients or circuit sharing, and Proposition 5.1 does not bridge that gap as written. 'NTP-useless' is defined relative to a chosen feature, prefix, and immediate target; nonlinear or distributed features can be missed by the linear-probe and SAE interfaces.

method.core_idea: Explain representation emergence developmentally by partitioning the gradients that can create a feature, rather than only assigning that feature a function in the final model.
method.mechanism: A stop-gradient cut at one layer-position divides total next-token loss into immediate direct paths, later-token paths that reuse the local residual through attention, and all other paths induced by shared parameters. Myopic and position-untied training selectively remove the latter two learning routes. Linear probes define feature directions, and exact-trajectory replay integrates each Adam-adjusted component's directional effect on mismatch to the final representation. Controlled Majority, Conditioned Majority, Othello, and TinyStories models test the decomposition. For Gemma 2, where replay is infeasible, SAE ablations yield Q(w), a ratio of delayed to immediate KL sensitivity, and automated labels, steering, and look-ahead subspace alignment characterize high-Q features.
assumptions: The selected layer-position stop-gradient cut gives semantically meaningful direct, pre-cached, and shared categories.
Myopic and m-untied training selectively remove the intended gradient routes without creating dominant unrelated optimization artifacts.
Final linear-probe directions are valid feature definitions throughout a replayed training trajectory.
Identical initialization, data order, and pseudorandom state reproduce the relevant Adam training path closely enough for attribution.
Sharing Adam's second moment while partitioning first moments is a defensible attribution of a nonlinear adaptive optimizer update.
Pearson correlation from linear probes captures the task-relevant representation, including Othello board state.
SAE feature ablation remains sufficiently on-manifold and the SAE faithfully reconstructs the relevant residual stream.

The Jacobian Gram metric at the selected residual cut cancels between direct and pre-cached directions; this unproved condition is required in addition to first-order and perfect-fit assumptions for Proposition 5.1's influence-ratio claim.
Automatically generated feature descriptions and model-based classifications reliably identify formal reasoning semantics.
Alignment with a linear look-ahead map's singular subspace measures a feature's contribution to future-token information.

techniques.role: Partitions total next-token gradient into direct, pre-cached, and shared terms at a layer-position cut.
Stops cross-position gradients through K/V paths to ablate pre-caching incentives.
Uses separate parameter copies across a sequence split to ablate circuit sharing while retaining forward attention.
Measures how a component update moves a probed feature toward its final representation.
Retrains with identical initialization and data order after final probe directions are known.
Partitions first moments by gradient source under a shared adaptive learning rate.
Labels features by whether they affect the immediate target, such as Othello legal moves.
Computes the delayed-to-immediate ablation-KL ratio Q(w); the audit treats it as a descriptive intervention statistic because the claimed gradient-influence equivalence is not proved.
Classifies SAE descriptions into code/math/syntax categories and validates with steering.
Compares SAE directions with singular subspaces of linear future-token predictors.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer Majority and Conditioned Majority models, ten seeds, tied/10-untied crossed with myopic/non-myopic training
evaluations.metric: Linear-probe Pearson correlation and first output-token accuracy
evaluations.result: Removing both pre-caching and sharing weakens locally useless features; myopic Conditioned Majority remains near 0.76 while non-myopic variants reach 0.99-1.00
evaluations.baseline: Standard tied non-myopic Transformer and each single ablation

evaluations.setting: OthelloGPT with 6 layers, width 256, 5.12 million synthetic games, one seed
evaluations.metric: Board-cell probe correlation and integrated influence intervals for useful versus useless occupied cells
evaluations.result: NTP-useful cells probe better; direct influence is positive only for useful cells, while pre-cached and shared paths support useless cells; the sole myopic run is unstable and fails to match ordinary-model convergence
evaluations.baseline: NTP-useful versus legal-move-invariant NTP-useless cells and myopic training curves

evaluations.setting: Four-layer width-128 TinyStories models, 256,000 samples, length 64, ten seeds
evaluations.metric: NTP loss, POS/dependency/original-position probe correlation, and component influence
evaluations.result: Myopic loss 3.29 plus or minus 0.02 versus 2.53 plus or minus 0.10; syntax remains mainly direct, while story position receives pre-cached influence in middle layers

evaluations.setting: Gemma-2-2B layer-15 Gemma Scope SAE, 16,384 features with 14,565 retained after effect filtering
evaluations.metric: Q(w), the ratio of delayed to immediate KL effect after feature ablation
evaluations.result: Formal-labeled features have heavier Q tails: fitted log-normal sigma 1.63 plus or minus 0.03 versus 1.23 plus or minus 0.02
evaluations.baseline: Features not classified as code, math, syntax, or text structure

evaluations.setting: Sixty-four unconditional 20-token generations per steered Gemma SAE feature at coefficient 10
evaluations.result: High-Q steering produces more code and punctuation; low-Q steering shows no symmetric formal-reasoning effect
evaluations.baseline: Features below the median steering outcomes and low-Q tail

evaluations.setting: Linear Gemma look-ahead maps trained on Pile residuals for distances through five future tokens
evaluations.metric: Correlation between Q(w) and alignment of SAE directions with leading look-ahead singular subspaces
evaluations.result: Spearman and Pearson curves are generally weak or negative but rank-dependent and sometimes approach or cross zero; no uncertainty or significance test is reported

evaluations.setting: Formal proofs at a fixed layer-position cut and local final-checkpoint intervention
evaluations.metric: Exact gradient identity and approximate influence ratio
evaluations.result: Proposition 3.1 is an exact algebraic decomposition; Proposition 5.1 is not established because its proof drops the non-scalar Jacobian Gram metric before equating influence and intervention-loss ratios
evaluations.baseline: Undecomposed training gradients and full trajectory attribution

limitations: Author-acknowledged: exact attribution requires replaying training and is computationally impractical for large models.
Author-acknowledged: the final-checkpoint Gemma analysis can inspect only a local region, not the full developmental path.
Reviewer-identified: NTP-uselessness is relative to an investigator-defined feature, prefix, and immediate prediction, not an intrinsic property of a representation.
Reviewer-identified: linear probes and one SAE dictionary can miss nonlinear, distributed, or superposed representations.
Reviewer-identified: myopic and m-untied models change optimization and function class, so performance gaps are not perfectly selective causal interventions on one learning route.
Reviewer-identified: the Adam partition is not unique because component first moments share a second-moment denominator containing interactions among all gradients.
Reviewer-identified: exact trajectory replay is fragile to nondeterministic kernels and defines features using a final model learned in the first run.
Reviewer-identified: Othello uses one model seed, only 16 central squares at every fourth position for influence, and the appendix calls results noisy and nonstationary.
Reviewer-identified: the myopic Othello run is visibly unstable and does not reach the ordinary model's loss or accuracy, confounding a selective pre-caching interpretation.
Reviewer-identified: Othello probe scores include empty cells and use regression/Pearson correlation, making direct numerical comparison with prior classifiers difficult.
Reviewer-identified: the claim that pre-caching is required for coherent text relies on loss from tiny four-layer TinyStories models and lacks blinded human or model-independent coherence evaluation.

Reviewer-identified: Proposition 5.1 additionally requires an unproved cancellation of the residual Jacobian Gram metric; first-order behavior and perfect fit alone do not make Q(w) a gradient-influence ratio.

Reviewer-identified: the appendix replaces the original residual with an SAE-decoded ablation, so dictionary reconstruction error and non-orthogonal feature interactions can contribute to every KL numerator and denominator.
Reviewer-identified: feature semantics pass through two model judgments—GPT-generated descriptions and GPT-4.1-nano labels—with no human validation or correction for classification error.
Reviewer-identified: high-Q tail enrichment includes both very high and very low extremes, while the steering effect is asymmetric and strongest only for high Q.

Reviewer-identified: the look-ahead correlations concern a linear predictor and SAE directions, are rank-dependent and near zero over parts of the plots, and have no uncertainty analysis; they do not resolve nonlinear or distributed planning information.
failure_modes: A feature classified as locally useless can be correlated with another variable that directly helps next-token prediction, invalidating the label.
Gradient stopping can prevent useful multi-layer circuits and raise loss so broadly that probe differences cease to isolate pre-caching.
Parameter untying can reduce data sharing, change capacity, and create distribution boundaries at the split position.
Final probe directions can rotate during training, making early influence on the final axis misrepresent feature formation.
Optimizer-component attribution can change under another valid decomposition of Adam's moments or weight decay.
One Othello seed can make unstable training dynamics look like a general gradient mechanism.
Linear probe correlation can reward decodable board information that the model does not causally use.
SAE ablation and decode can perturb many entangled features or introduce reconstruction error, inflating delayed KL effects.

An anisotropic residual-to-parameter Jacobian can rotate or reweight direct and pre-cached loss directions differently, invalidating the paper's conversion from activation KL ratios to parameter-gradient influence ratios.
A tiny immediate KL denominator can make Q(w) extreme even when the absolute future effect is modest; filtering only partly controls this.
Automated feature descriptions can create circular semantics when the same high-activation examples drive both description and claimed enrichment.
Steering at every generated position with a large coefficient can create code-like artifacts unrelated to the feature's ordinary function.
Negative linear look-ahead alignment can miss nonlinear or distributed anticipatory computation.
reusable_insights: Separate the causal role of a final feature from the gradient routes that made it emerge.
Use stop-gradient identities to define an exhaustive path partition before attaching semantic interpretations to attribution scores.
Cross training interventions with within-run attribution; agreement is more informative than either alone.
Test locally useless features in tasks where immediate target sufficiency can be computed exactly, such as legal-move equivalence classes.
Preserve exact seeds and data order when replaying development, and quantify replay divergence before integrating influence.
Treat a future-effect ratio as a descriptive local intervention statistic unless the parameter-space metric linking it to gradient influence is established.
Control ratio metrics for absolute numerator and denominator magnitude to prevent tail artifacts.
Validate model-generated feature labels with blinded human samples and steering or patching interventions.
Distinguish pre-caching from look-ahead: information useful to later computation need not encode a future token explicitly.
Report seed count and position-wise nonstationarity when developmental attributions vary over sequence time.
open_questions: Can gradient provenance be estimated online in one training run without storing every component or replaying the trajectory?
Can Proposition 5.1 be repaired by measuring influence in activation space or explicitly retaining and estimating the Jacobian Gram metric?
How sensitive are direct/pre-cached/shared attributions to the chosen layer-position cut and optimizer decomposition?
Do the Othello influence patterns replicate across many seeds, model sizes, nonlinear probes, and legal-move-equivalent counterfactual boards?
Which semantic features, rather than original-story position, explain the TinyStories loss gap under myopic training?
Does pre-caching remain necessary in large language models after matching compute and compensating for myopic optimization difficulty?
Can circuit-sharing gradients be isolated in a pretrained large model with parameter-local or data-attribution approximations?
Are high-Q code features causally needed for multi-step code generation, syntax checking, or algorithm execution?
How stable is Q(w) across corpora, activation thresholds, SAE sizes, layers, and intervention magnitudes?
Do human-validated feature labels preserve the reported formal-reasoning tail enrichment?
Can nonlinear look-ahead decoders reverse the negative relation between pre-caching degree and future-token information?
Does multi-token prediction alter the balance among direct, pre-cached, and shared feature-development signals?
Can gradient-origin signatures predict whether a representation will be robust under distribution or length shift?

competitive_landscape.title: Do Language Models Plan Ahead for Future Tokens?
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu et al. introduce myopic training and distinguish pre-caching from breadcrumb explanations of look-ahead at model and task scale. This paper reuses myopic training but adds circuit sharing, an exact three-way gradient partition, per-feature trajectory attribution, and a large-model SAE proxy.

competitive_landscape.title: Future Lens: Anticipating Subsequent Tokens from a Single Hidden State
competitive_landscape.difference: Future Lens decodes and intervenes on future-token predictions already present in static hidden states. This paper asks which training paths create individual features and finds that high delayed causal effect is negatively related to its linear look-ahead subspace.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent World Representations: Exploring a Sequence Model Trained on a Synthetic Task
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. establish linear Othello board representations and causal interventions in a trained model. This paper accepts that testbed but partitions cells by immediate legal-move utility and attributes their unequal emergence to direct, pre-cached, and shared gradients.

competitive_landscape.title: Evaluating the World Model Implicit in a Generative Model
competitive_landscape.difference: Vafa et al. use Myhill-Nerode-style state equivalence and counterfactual tests to show that generative world models can be incoherent despite decodable state. This paper offers a developmental explanation for the Othello fragility but does not replace those stronger behavioral coherence tests.

competitive_landscape.title: The Pitfalls of Next-Token Prediction
competitive_landscape.difference: Bachmann and Nagarajan construct tasks where teacher-forced next-token prediction learns undesirable shortcuts or cannot elicit planning and motivate alternative objectives. This paper shows why standard NTP can nevertheless create immediately useless features through later-position and shared-parameter gradients.

competitive_landscape.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
competitive_landscape.difference: Gloeckle et al. add several future-token prediction heads and show gains in code and induction, directly modifying the supervision signal. This paper leaves ordinary NTP unchanged and decomposes the implicit future and shared gradient routes it already contains.

competitive_landscape.title: The Belief State Transformer
competitive_landscape.difference: The Belief State Transformer uses prefix and suffix information to train compact predictive belief states and evaluates state sufficiency. This paper diagnoses how decoder-only NTP features emerge without a bidirectional auxiliary objective and makes the narrower claim that non-direct gradients can create locally useless representations.

competitive_landscape.title: Crosscoding Through Time: Tracking Emergence & Consolidation Of Linguistic Representations Throughout LLM Pretraining
competitive_landscape.difference: Crosscoding Through Time aligns sparse features across real LLM checkpoints and uses Relative Indirect Effects to identify when linguistic features become causally important, directly competing on feature development rather than static interpretation. It scales through saved checkpoints and causal mediation but does not decompose the NTP gradient into direct, pre-cached, and shared paths; this paper offers finer gradient provenance on small replayable models but a weaker large-model bridge.

competitive_landscape.title: Tracking the Feature Dynamics in LLM Training: A Mechanistic Study
competitive_landscape.difference: SAE-Track follows semantic formation and directional drift across a continual series of sparse autoencoders, providing direct evidence that feature axes evolve during training. That evidence challenges this paper's assumption that a final probe direction can stand in for the feature throughout replay; conversely, SAE-Track describes feature trajectories without attributing them to direct, future-position, or shared-parameter gradient paths.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Seemingly useless Transformer features arise through two non-direct learning routes—pre-caching for future positions and circuit sharing across positions—and a three-way gradient decomposition can attribute their development in toy tasks, Othello, language, and Gemma 2.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Proposition 3.1 gives an exact path decomposition, and crossed myopic/untied interventions plus trajectory replay provide small-model evidence for direct, pre-cached, and shared contributions. Othello and TinyStories expose task-specific signatures. Gemma SAE ablations reveal a reproducible delayed/immediate-effect statistic with formal-structure enrichment, but Proposition 5.1 does not prove that statistic is a gradient-influence ratio, and the look-ahead correlations are weak and rank-dependent rather than uniformly negative.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The credible novelty is not myopic training, future-state probing, checkpoint feature tracking, or SAE feature dynamics, all of which have direct prior art. It is the exact three-way stop-gradient identity at a chosen layer-position cut, the addition of circuit sharing as a developmental route, and small-model trajectory attribution to those components. Large-model claims must be narrowed: Q(w) is an empirical local intervention ratio because the Proposition 5.1 proof incorrectly cancels a Jacobian Gram metric; low-Q steering is null; and the linear look-ahead plots do not justify a general planning conclusion. Altered training regimes, final-axis probes, one-seed Othello evidence, and a non-unique Adam accounting further limit causal scope.

reviewer_notes: Independent secondary verification read all 27 pages of the exact pinned arXiv:2603.14087v1 PDF end to end, including both propositions, every displayed derivation, Tables 1-9, Figures 1-20, references, hyperparameters, noisy Othello position plots, TinyStories statistics, SAE filtering/labeling/steering, and both Spearman and Pearson look-ahead panels. A fresh explicit v1 download matched the indexed PDF SHA-256 1fdcf269bedcbeeb480156cbba6e9fbe7e630a6c1d16262c651c719e6e0d7a71 byte for byte; source_provenance remains index-derived. This pass corrected a substantive formal omission: Equation 10's Jacobian Gram matrix does not generally cancel, so Proposition 5.1 does not establish Q(w) as a gradient-influence ratio. It also records the myopic Othello convergence failure, null low-Q steering result, and weak/rank-dependent look-ahead correlations rather than repeating the prose's stronger claims. Nine official primary arXiv records spanning myopic training, look-ahead, Othello state, world-model coherence, NTP objectives, belief states, and developmental feature tracking were independently opened and exact-version checked on 2026-08-23.

The audit preserves novelty only for the three-way cut, circuit-sharing route, and small-model gradient provenance.
